G5500.d:
χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ
 (χείρ, τείνω) 
  1. to vote by stretching out the hand in the Athenian ἐκκλησία (Luc., Plut.). 
  2. to appoint: 
  (a) by vote, 2 Cor.8:19 
  (b) without vote, Acts.14:23 (see Rackham, in l) (cf. προχειροτονέω).†
 (AS)

G5501.d:
χείρων, -ον, compar. of κακός 
 [in LXX: 1Ki.17:43 B, Wis.15:18 17:6, 3Ma.5:20 * ;] 
worse: Matt.9:16 12:45 27:64, Mark.2:21, Luke.11:26, John.5:14, 1 Tim.5:8, Heb.10:29, 2 Pet.2:20; εἰς (ἐπὶ) τὸ χεῖρον, Mark.5:26, 2 Tim.3:13.†
 (AS)

G5502.d:
Χερουβείν (Rec. -βίμ), τά (Heb. כְּרוּב), 
 Cherubim: Heb.9:6 (cf. Exod.25:17 (18), al.; see DB, i, 377 ff.).†
 (AS)

G5503.d:
χήρα, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for אַלְמָנָה ;] 
a widow: Matt.23:13 (Rec., R, mg.), Mark.12:40-43, Luke.2:37 4:25 7:12 18:3, 5 20:47 21:2-3, Acts.6:1 9:39, 41, 1 Cor.7:8, 1 Tim.5:3-5 5:11 5:16, Jas.1:27; γυνὴ χ., Luke.4:26; of one of an ordo viduarum (see CGT, in l), 1 Tim.5:9; metaphorically, of a city forsaken, Rev.18:7.†
 (AS)

G5504.d:
ἐχθές
 (Rec. χθές), adv., [in LXX for תְּמוֹל, etc. ;] 
yesterday: John.4:52, Acts.7:28, Heb.13:8 (on the form, see Rutherford, NPhr., 370 f.).†
 ἐχθές, 
 adverb ={χθές}, yesterday, ( 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 175, “Th.” 616, etc.; ἀπ᾽ ἐ. “Anthologia Graeca” 11.35 (1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus); μέσφα τό γ᾽ ἐ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.144 ); οὐ γάρ τι νῦν γε κἀ. today or yesterday, ( 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 456; οὐκ ἐ. οὐδὲ πρῴην 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 58 ); ἐ. καὶ τρίτης [ἡμέρας] ( LXX.Ruth.2.11, compare 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 10.7. (ἐχθές is commoner than χθές) in Comedy texts and LXX, is the only form used in “NT”, and frequently in papyri of all periods, ( “PSI” 4.442.21 (3rd c.BC), etc.)) (AS)

G5505.d:
χιλιάς, -άδος, ἡ
 (χίλιοι), [in LXX for אֶלֶף ;] 
the number one thousand, a thousand: Luke.14:31, Acts.4:4, 1 Cor.10:8, Rev.5:11 7:4-8 11:13 14:1, 3 21:16.†
 (AS)

G5506.d:
χιλίαρχος (in Hdt., al., -ης), -ου, ὁ 
 (χίλιοι, ἄρχω) [in LXX chiefly for אַלּוּף שַׂר ;] 
a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand, esp. a Roman military tribune, the commander of a cohort: John.18:12, Acts.21:31-33, 37 22:24-29 23:10, 15 23:17-19, 22 24:7, 22 25:23; more generally, of officers of similar rank, Mark.6:21, Rev.6:15 19:18 (see, DB, i, 352b; DCG, i, 271a, 307a).†
 (AS)

G5508.d:
χίος, -ου, ἡ 
 Chios, an island in Ægean Sea: Acts.20:15.†
 (AS)

G5509.d:
χιτών, ῶνος, ὁ
 [in LXX chiefly for כְּתֹנֶת:] 
the garment worn next the skin (though two tunics were sometimes worn, see Swete, Mk., 117), a tunic: Matt.10:10, Mark.6:9 14:63, Luke.3:11 9:3, Ju 23; dieting. from ἱμάτιον (which see), Matt.5:40, Luke.6:29, John.19:23, Acts.9:39 (see DCG, i, 338, 340, 499) 
 (AS)

G5510.d:
χιών, -όνος, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג ;] 
snow: Matt.28:3, Rev.1:14.†
 (AS)

G5511.d:
χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.12:35 * ;] 
a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (which see): Matt.27:28, 31 (see Tr., Syn., § 1).†
 (AS)

G5512.d:
χλευάζω
 (χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wis.11:14, 2Ma.7:7, 4Ma.5:22 * ;] 
to jest, mock, jeer: Acts.17:32.†
 (AS)

G5513.d:
χλιαρός, -ά, -όν
 (χλίω, to become warm), 
warm, tepid; metaphorically, of persons, luke-warm: Rev.3:16.†
 (AS)

G5514.d:
Χλόη, -ης, ἡ
 (i.e. tender foliage), 
Chloe: 1 Cor.1:11.†
 (AS)

G5515.d:
χλωρός, -ά, -όν
 (χλόη), [in LXX for יֶרֶק, etc. ;] 
  (a) pale green: χόρτος, Mark.6:39, Rev.8:7; πᾶν χ., Rev.9:4; 
  (b) pale: ἵππος, Rev.6:8.†
 (AS)

G5516.d:
χξς ́
 (on ς, see: Z), in T, Tr., Rec. for ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ, 
six hundred and sixty-six (L, mg., R, mg., six hundred and sixteen), the mystical number of the Beast: Rev.13:18 (on the interpretation, see Swete, Ap., 172 f.).†
 (AS)

G5517.d:
χοϊκός, -ή, -όν,
 (χοῦς) 
earthy, made of dust: 1 Cor.15:47-49 (see Field, Notes, 179 f.).†
 (AS)

G5518.d:
χοῖνιξ, -ικος, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Eze.45:10-11 (בַּת) * ;] 
a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart: Rev.6:6 (EV, measure).†
 (AS)

G5520.d:
χολάω, -ῶ
 (χολή), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:1 R * ;] 
  1. to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.). 
  2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: with dative of person(s), John.7:23.†
 (AS)

G5521.d:
χολή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה ;] 
gall: Matt.27:34 (here prob. = myrrh, cf. Mark.15:23, see Swete, in l; DCG, i, 634); metaphorically, Acts.8:23.†
 (AS)

G5522.d:
χοῦς, -οός accusative, οῦν, ὁ, (contr. from χόος), 
 [in LXX chiefly for עָפָר ;] 
  1. earth, soil. 
  2. In later writers (Pint., LXX), = κονιορτός, dust: Mark.6:11, Rev.18:19.†
 (AS)

G5523.d:
Χοραζείν (Rec. -ζίν), ἡ, 
 Chorazin, a town of Galilee: Matt.11:21, Luke.10:13.†
 (AS)

G5524.d:
χορηγέω, -ῶ
 (χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;] 
  1. to lead a χορός (see LS, see word). 
  2. to defray the cost of a χορός. 
  3. In late writers, metaphorically, with accusative (see M, Pr., 65), to supply, furnish abundantly: 2 Cor.9:10, 1 Pet.4:11 (Polyb., al.).†
 (AS)

G5525.d:
χορός, -οῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָחוֹל, מְחֹלָה ;] 
a dance: pl., Luke.15:25.†
 (AS)

G5526.d:
χορτάζω 
 (χόρτος), [in LXX for שָׂבַע, Ps.17:14 al. ;] 
  (a) prop., of animals (see Lft. on Phil.4:12), to feed, fatten: Rev.19:21; 
  (b) in late Gk. (Kennedy, Sources, 82, 156), of persons, to fill or satisfy with food: with accusative of person(s), Matt.15:33; pass., Matt.14:20 15:37, Mark.6:42 7:27 8:8, Luke.9:17, John.6:26, Jas.2:16; opposite to πεινᾶν, Phil.4:12; with genitive of thing(s), Mark.8:4; ἀπό, Luke.16:21; ἐκ, Luke.15:16, WH, txt.; metaphorically, Matt.5:6, Luke.6:21.†
 (AS)

G5527.d:
χόρτασμα, -τος, τό
 (χορτάζω), [in LXX: Gen.24:25, 32 42:27 43:24, Jdg.19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), Deu.11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Sir.33:24) Sir.38:26 * ;] 
fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Acts.7:11 (RV, sustenance).†
 (AS)

G5528.d:
χόρτος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for עֶשֶׂב, also for חָצִיר, etc. ;] 
  1. an enclosure, a feeding place (Hom.). 
  2. food, esp. for cattle, grass: Matt.13:26 14:19, Mark.4:28 6:39, Luke.12:28, John.6:10, 1 Cor.3:12, Jas.1:10-11, 1 Pet.1:24" (LXX), Rev.9:4; χ. χλωρός, Mark.6:39, Rev.8:7.†
 (AS)

G5530.d:
χράομαι, χρῶμαι
 (χρή), [in LXX for עָשָׂה, etc. ;] 
to use, make use of: with dative (cf. M, Pr., 64, 158), Acts.27:17, 1 Cor.9:12 9:15, 1 Tim.1:8 5:23; μᾶλλον χρῆσαι (i.e. the opportunity; see M, Pr., 247), 1 Cor.7:21; as some­times in late writers (cf. M, Pr., 64; Lft., Notes, 233), with accusative, 1 Cor.7:31; of feelings, etc., to exercise, shew: 2 Cor.1:17 3:12; with adv., ἀποτόμως, to deal sharply, 2 Cor.13:10; with dative of person(s) (cl.), to treat, deal with, Acts.27:3.†
 (AS)

G5531.d:
χράω, κίχρημι 
 [in LXX for לָוָה, etc. ;] 
to lend: Luke.11:5.†
 (AS)

G5532.d:
χρεία, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX: 2Ch.2:16 (15) (צֹרֶךְ), Est.7:20 (חַשְׁחוּת) frequently in Sir.1:1-30 -2 Mac ;] 
  1. need, necessity: Acts.28:10, Titus.3:14; πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χ. (RV, txt., for edifying as the need may be; but see Field, Notes, 192), Eph.4:29; ἕστι χ., Luke.10:42, Heb.7:11; χ. ἔχειν, with genitive, Matt.6:8 21:3, Mark.11:3, Luke.9:11 15:7 19:31, 34 22:71, John.13:29, 1 Cor.12:21 12:24, 1 Thess.4:12, Heb.10:36, Rev.21:23 22:5; before τοῦ, with inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), Heb.5:12; absol. (sc. genitive), Acts.2:45 4:35; with genitive of person(s), Matt.9:12 26:65, Mark.2:17 14:63, Luke.5:31; with inf. (Bl., § 69, 5), Matt.3:14 14:16, John.13:10, 1 Thess.1:8 4:9; before ἵνα, John.16:30, 1 John.2:27; absol., Mark.2:25, Eph.4:28, 1 John.3:17; οὐδὲν χ. ἔχειν, Rev.3:17; ἡ χ., with genitive subjc., Phil.2:25 4:16, 19; pl., Acts.20:34, Rom.12:13. 
  2. matter, business (so esp. in late writers, Polyb., al.; 1Ma.12:45, al.): Acts.6:3.†
 (AS)

G5533.d:
χρεοφειλέτης (Rec. χρεω-, WH, χρεοφιλ-; see WH, App., 152, 154), -ου, ὁ, 
 (χρέος, a debt, + ὀφειλέτης) [in LXX: Job.31:37, Pro.29:13 * ;] 
a debtor: Luke.7:41 16:5.†
 (AS)

G5534.d:
χρή  impers. 
 (χράω, see LS, see word), 
it is necessary: Jas.3:10 (cf. δεῖ.).†
 (AS)

G5535.d:
χρῄζω
 (χρή) [in LXX Jdg.11:7, 1Ki.17:18 A * ;] 
to need, have need of: with genitive of thing(s), Matt.6:32, Luke.11:8 12:30, 2 Cor.3:1; with genitive of person(s) before ἐν, Rom.16:2.†
 (AS)

G5536.d:
χρῆμα, -τος, τό
 (χράομαι) [in LXX: Jos.22:8, 2Ch.1:11-12 (נֶכֶס), Job.27:17 (כֶּסֶף), etc.; frequently in Sir (5:1, 8, al.), 2 and 4 Mac ;] 
a thing that one uses or needs (and generally, a matter, event, business); hence in pl., 
  (a) wealth, riches: οἱ τά χ. ἔχοντες, Mark.10:23-24, Luke.18:24; 
  (b) money: Acts.8:18, 20 24:26; sing. (rare in cl.) of a special sum of money, Acts.4:37.†
 (AS)

G5537.d:
χρηματίζω
 (χρῆμα), [in LXX: Jer.26:2 29:23 30:2 36:2, 4 A (דָבַר pi.), Jer.25:30) (שָׁאַג), 3Ki.18:27, Job.40:8 * ;] 
  1. to transact business, hence, to consult, deliberate (Thuc., Dem., al.); hence in later writers, 
  2. to make answer (esp. of offcial pronounce­ments by magistrates, etc.; in π. of the royal reply to an ἔντευξις, which see; cf. Deiss., BS, 122); of an answer by an oracle (Died., Plut., al.); in FlJ, LXX and NT, of divine communications, to instruct, admonish,  warn: pass. (Bl., § 54, 3), Matt.2:22, Heb.8:5 11:7 12:25; with inf. (Bl., § 69,4; 70, 3; 72, 5), Matt.2:12, Luke.2:26, Acts.10:22 
  3. to assume a name (as in business), be called (Polyb., al.): Acts.11:26, Rom.7:3 (gnomic fut.; cf. Burton, § 69).†
 (AS)

G5538.d:
χρηματισμός, -οῦ), ὁ
 (χρηματίζω, which see), [in LXX: Pro.31:1 (מַשָּׂא), 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 11:17 * ;] 
a divine response, an oracle: Rom.11:4 (Xen., Plat., al.).†
 (AS)

G5539.d:
χρήσιμος, -η, -ον
 (χράομαι), [in LXX: Gen.37:26 בֶּצַע etc. ;] 
useful: 2 Tim.2:14.†
 (AS)

G5540.d:
χρῆσις, -εως, ἡ
 (χράομαι), [in LXX: 1Ki.1:28 (שָׁאַל), Sir.18:8, al. ;] 
use: in a sexual sense, Rom.1:26; with genitive obj., θηλείας, Rom.1:27 (for exx., see Thayer, see word).†
 (AS)

G5542.d:
χρηστολογία, -ας, ἡ
 (χρηστός, λέγω), 
fair speaking: in bad sense, Rom.16:18 (in good sense also, eccl.).†
 (AS)

G5544.d:
χρηστότης, -ητος, ἡ
 (χρηστός), [in LXX for טוּב and cogn. forms ;] 
  1. goodness, excellence, uprightness: Rom.3:12 (LXX). 
  2. goodness of heart, kindness: Rom.2:4, 2 Cor.6:6, Gal.5:22, Col.3:12, Titus.3:4; before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Eph.2:7; id., opposite to ἀποτομία, Rom.11:22. 
 SYN.: see: ἀγαθωσύνη. (AS)

G5545.d:
χρίσμα (T, χρῖσμα, as in cl.; see Tdf., Pr., 102; Bl., § 4, 2), -τος, το 
 (χρίω), 
later form of χρῖμα (Æsch., al.), 
 [in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms (Exod.29:7, al.) ;] 
an anointing, unction (the result of the action χρίειν; ICC, in l; but cf. Westc., in l, for the view that the oil, not the act, is meant): 1 John.2:20 Jn 2:27.†
 (AS)

G5546.d:
Χριστιανός (D, Χρεισ-; on the form Χρησ-, see Bl., § 3, 6; 27, 4 on the ending, -ανος, see Bl., ll. with; Deiss., LAE, 382), -οῦ ὁ, 
 a Christian, the name first given to the disciples by pagan gentiles at Antioch: Acts.11:26 26:28, 1 Pet.4:16 (see reff. in Thayer, see word; also DB, i, 384).†
 (AS)

G5547.d:
χριστός (Χρ-), -ή, -όν 
 (χρίω), [in LXX for מָשִׁיחַ and cogn. forms ;] 
  1. 1. as adj., 
  (a) of things, anointing, to be used as ointment (Æsch., Eur., al.; τ. ἔλαιον τὸ χ., Lev.21:10); 
  (b) of persons, anointed (ὁ ἰερεὺς ὁ χ., Lev.4:5; οἱ χ. ἰευρεῖς, 2Ma.1:10): ὁ χ. τοῦ κυρίου or Θεοῦ (1Ki.2:10, Ps.2:2, al.), of the Messiah (Aram., מְשִׁיחָא; cf. Dalman, Words, 289 ff.), Luke.2:11, 26 John.1:41, Acts.2:36 4:26, al. 
  2. As subst., ὁ Χριστός, the Messiah, the Christ: Matt.2:4, Mark.8:29, Luke.2:11, John.1:20, Acts.2:31, Rom.7:4, al.; Ἰησοῦς, Mark.1:1, John.1:17, Acts.2:38, al.; Χ. Ἰησοῦς, Matt.1:18, WH, mg.  Acts.5:42, Rom.6:3, al.; Χ. κύριος, Luke.2:11; Ἰησοῦς Χ. ὁ κύριος, Acts.15:26, Rom.1:7, al. 
 (AS)

G5548.d:
χρίω 
 to anoint (Hom., al.); 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָשַׁח of consecration to a sacred office: priest, Exod.28:41; prophet, 3Ki.19:16; king, 1Ki.10:1; of things, Exod.40:9, Lev.8:10, al.]. 
In NT, metaphorically, of God's anointing, 
  (a) Christ: Acts.4:27; with inf., Luke.4:18 (LXX); with dupl. accusative (see B1., § 34, 4), Heb.1:9 (LXX); πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, Acts.10:38; 
  (b) Christians: 2 Cor.1:21 (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 73) (cf. ἐν-, ἐπι-Χριω).†
 SYN: see: ἀλείφω 
 (AS)

G5549.d:
χρονίζω
 (χρόνος), [in LXX chiefly for אָחַר pi. ;] 
to spend or take time, to tarry, linger, delay: Matt.24:48 25:5, Heb.10:37; before ἐν, with dative loc., Luke.1:21; with inf., Luke.12:45.†
 (AS)

G5550.d:
χρόνος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for יוֹם, also for עֵת, etc. ;] 
time (a space of time, whether long or short; cf. Lft., Notes, 70): Matt.2:7, Mark.9:21, Luke.1:57, Acts.3:21 7:17, 23 13:18 17:30 27:9, Heb.11:32, 1 Pet.1:17 4:3, Rev.10:6; στιγμὴ χρόνου, Luke.4:5; πλήρωμα τοῦ χ., Gal.4:4; ποιεῖν χ., Acts.15:33 18:23; βιῶσαι, 1 Pet.4:2; διδόναι, Rev.2:21; pl., χ. καὶ (ἢ) καιροί (Lft., l.with), Acts.1:7, 1 Thess.5:1; ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάτου τῶν χ. (χρόνου), 1 Pet.1:20, Ju 18; with prep., ἄχρι, Acts.3:21; διὰ τὸν χ., Heb.5:12; ἐν χ., Acts.1:6, 21; ἐπὶ (πλείονα) χ., Luke.18:4, Acts.18:20; ἐφ᾽ ὅσον χ., Rom.7:1, 1 Cor.7:39, Gal.4:1; κατὰ τὸν χ., Matt.2:16; μετὰ τολὺν (τοσοῦτον) χ., Matt.25:19, Heb.4:7; πρὸ χ. αἰωςίων, 2 Tim.1:9, Titus.1:2, instr. dative of extension of time (see M, Pr., 75, 148; Deiss., LAE, 206), Luke.8:27, 29 John.14:9, Acts.8:11, Rom.16:25; accusative, of duration of time, Mark.2:19, Luke.20:9, John.5:6 7:33 12:35 14:9, Acts.14:3, 28 19:22 20:18, 1 Cor.16:7, Rev.6:11.†
 SYN.: see: καιρός  (AS)

G5551.d:
χρονοτριβέω, -ῶ
 (χρόνος, τρίβω), 
to spend time: Acts.20:16.†
 (AS)

G5552.d:
Χρύσεος, -εα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν; on accusative sing. fem., -ᾶν, Rev.1:13 and genitive pl. uncontr., -εων, Rev.2:1, LTr., see M, Pr., 48 and cf. Thackeray, Gr., x, 172 f.)
 (χρυσός), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;] 
golden, i.e. made or overlaid with gold: 2 Tim.2:20, Heb.9:4, Rev.1:12-13, 20 2:1 4:4 5:8 8:3 9:13, 20 14:14 15:6-7 17:4 21:15.†
 (AS)

G5553.d:
χρυσίον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of χρυσός, which see), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;] 
a piece of gold, gold: 1 Cor.3:12, Heb.9:4, 1 Pet.1:7, Rev.3:18 21:18, 21; of golden ornaments, 1 Tim.2:9 (WH, txt., RV), 1 Pet.3:3, Rev.17:4 18:16 (WH, txt., R); of gold coin, money, Acts.3:6 20:33, 1 Pet.1:18.†
 (AS)

G5554.d:
χρυσο-δακτύλιος, -ον 
 with a gold ring: Jas.2:2.†
 (AS)

G5555.d:
χρυσό-λιθος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Exod.28:20 36:20 (Exod.39:13), Eze.28:13 (תַּרְשִׁישׁ) * ;] 
a chrysolite (on its identification, see Swete, Ap., 288 f.; DB, iv, 620): Rev.21:20.†
 (AS)

G5556.d:
χρυσό-πρασος, -ου, ὁ 
 a chrysoprase (see Swete, Ap., 289): Rev.21:20.†
 (AS)

G5557.d:
χρυσός, -οῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;] 
gold: Matt.2:11, Rev.9:7; of golden ornaments, Matt.23:16-17, 1 Tim.2:9 (Rec., WH, mg.), Jas.5:3, Rev.17:4 (Rec., WH, mg.) Rev.18:12, 16 (Rec., WH, mg.); of images, Acts.17:29; of gold coin, Matt.10:9.†
 (AS)

G5558.d:
χρυσόω, -ῶ
 (χρυσός) [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה pi. ;] 
to gild, cover with gold: pass., with dative, χρυσίῳ (pleonast., cf. Exod.26:37), Rev.17:4 18:16.†
 (AS)

G5559.d:
χρώς, genitive, χρωτός, ὁ
 [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;] 
in cl. rare in prose, the surface of the body, skin: Acts.19:12.†
 (AS)

G5560.d:
χωλός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX for פִּסֵּחַ ;] 
lame, halt, maimed: Matt.11:5 15:30-31 18:8 21:14, Mark.9:45, Luke.7:22 14:13, 21, John.5:3, Acts.3:2 8:7 14:8, Heb.12:13.†
 (AS)

G5561.d:
χώρα, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX for אֶרֶץ, מְדִינָה, etc. ;] 
  1. most frequently in cl., a space, place. 
  2. land, i.e. 
  (a) a land, country, region: Matt.12:2, Mark.5:10 6:55, Luke.2:8 15:13-15 19:12, John.11:54, Acts.13:49 27:27; χ. Γαλατική, Acts.16:6 18:23; Τραχωνίτιδος, Luke.3:1; τ. Ἰουδαίας, Acts.26:20; τ. Ἰουδαίων, Acts.10:39; pl., τῆς Ἰουδαίας κ. Σαμαρείας, Acts.8:1; Γεργεσηνῶν (Γερασηνῶν, Γαδαρηνῶν) Matt.8:28, Mark.5:1, Luke.8:26; ἐν χ. καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου, Matt.4:16; 
  (b) land, property: Luke.12:16; 
  (with) the country, opposite to the town; so in pl., Luke.21:21, John.4:35, Jas.5:4.†
 SYN.: ἄγρος, τόπος (cf. DCG, i, 591a; LS, see word χώρα, ad init.).  (AS)

G5562.d:
χωρέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Gen.13:6 (נָשָׂא), 3Ki.7:26 7:38 (כּוּל hi.), 2Ch.4:5 (חָזַק hi.), Wis.7:23-24, al. ;] 
  I. Intrans., 
  1. to make room, give way, retire, pass: before εἰς, Matt.15:17; metaphorically (EV, come), εἰς μετάνοιαν, 2 Pet.3:9. 
  2. to go forward, advance, progress (Plat., Polyb., al.) ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ. ἐν ὑμῖν, John.8:37 (R, txt., hath not free course; R, mg., hath no place, for WH. cf. Field, Notes, 94 f.). 
  II. Trans., to have space for holding, to hold: Mark.2:2 (cf. Ge, l.with), John.21:25; of measures (1Ki, 2Ch, ll. with), John.2:6. Metaphorical, of having or making room in mind or heart: Matt.19:11-12 (EV, receive), 2 Cor.7:2 (R, txt., open your hearts; mg., make room) (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ὑπο-χωρέω).†
 (AS)

G5563.d:
χωρίζω 
 [in LXX: 2Ch.12:8, al. (בָּדַל ni., etc.), Wis.1:3, 2Ma.5:21, al. ;] 
  1. to separate, divide, put asunder: with accusative of thing(s), opposite to συζεύγνυμι Matt.19:6, Mark.10:9; with accusative of person(s), before ἀπό (Wis.1:3), Rom.8:35, 39; pf. pass ptcp., Heb.7:26. 
  2. In late writers, mid. and 1 aor pass., to separate oneself, depart: Phm 15; before ἀπό Acts.1:4, ἐκ, Acts.18:1-2; of divorce (polyb., al.), 1 Cor.7:10-11 7:15 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-χωρίζω).†
 (AS)

G5564.d:
χωρίον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: 1Ch.27:27 (כֶּרֶם), 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:7 2Mac 12:21, 4Ma.15:20 * ;] 
  1. a place, region. 
  2. an estate, property, piece of land: Matt.26:36, Mark.14:32, John.4:5, Acts.1:18-19 4:34 5:3, 8 28:7.†
 (AS)

G5565.d:
χωρίς 
 adv., 
  1. separately, apart: John.20:7. 
  2. As prep., with genitive, 
  (a) separate from, apart from, without (practically equiv. to ἄνευ; see Field, Notes, 103): Matt.13:34, Mark.4:34, Luke.6:49, John.1:3 15:5, Rom.3:21, 28 4:6 7:8-9 10:14, 1 Cor.4:8 11:11, 2 Cor.12:3, Eph.2:12, Phil.2:14, 1 Tim.2:8 5:21, Phm 14, Heb.4:15 7:7, 20 9:7, 18 9:22, 28 10:25 11:6, 40 12:8, 14 (οὗ χωρίς; see Bl., § 82, 3), Jas.2:18, 20 2:26; 
  (b) besides: Matt.14:21 15:38, 2 Cor.11:28.†
 (AS)

G5566.d: the North-west wind , Lat. Caurus, (New Testament) (ML)

G5567.d:
ψάλλω 
 [in LXX chiefly for זָמַר pi. (Jdg.5:3, Ps.7:17, al.), also for נָגַן pi. (1Ki.16:16 ff, al.) ;] 
  1. to pull, twitch, twang (as a bowstring, etc.; Æsch., Eur., al.), hence, 
  2. absol., 
  (a) to play a stringed instrument with the fingers (Hdt., Plat., al.); 
  (b) later, to sing to a harp, sing psalms (LXX); in NT, to sing a hymn, sing praise: Jas.5:13; with dative of person(s), Rom.15:9 (LXX), Eph.5:19; dative instr., 1 Cor.14:15.†
 (AS)

G5568.d:
ψαλμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (ψάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for מִזְמוֹר ;] 
  1. a striking, twitching with the fingers (Eur., al.), hence, a striking of musical strings (Æsch., a1.), and hence in later writers, 
  2. a sacred song sung to musical accompaniment, a psalm (LXX): 1 Cor.14:26, Eph.5:19, Col.3:16; of OT psalms, Luke.24:44, Acts.13:33; βίβλος ψαλμῶν, Luke.20:42, Acts.1:20.†
 SYN.: see: ὕμνος  (AS)

G5569.d:
ψευδ-άδελφος, -ου, ὁ 
 a false brother: of professing Christians, 2 Cor.11:26, Gal.2:4.†
 (AS)

G5570.d:
ψευδ-απόστολος, -ου, ὁ

G5571.d:
ψευδής, -ές
 (ψεύδομαι), [in LXX for שֶׁקֶר, שָׁוְא, כָּזָב; etc. ;] 
lying, false, untrue (of persons and things): Rev.2:2; μάρτυρες, Acts.6:13; as subst., ὁ ψ., a liar: Rev.21:8.†
 (AS)

G5572.d:
ψευδο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ 
 a false teacher: 2 Pet.2:1.†

G5573.d:
ψευδο-λόγος, -ον

G5574.d:
ψεύδω  to deceive by lies; more frequently in the depon. mid, form ψεύδομαι (so always in NT), 
 [in LXX chiefly for כָּחַשׁ pi. ;] 
  1. absol., to lie: Heb.6:18, 1 John.1:6, Rev.3:9; οὐ ψεύδομαι, Rom.9:1, 2 Cor.11:31, Gal.1:20, 1 Tim.2:7 with dative of person(s) (Ps.18:45, John.5:12, al.), Acts.5:4; before εἰς, Col.3:9; κατά, Jas.3:14 (Hort, in l). 
  2. Like act., with accusative, to deceive by lies (Æsch., al.): Acts.5:3.†
 (AS)

G5575.d:
ψευδο-μάρτυς, -υρος, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Dan LXX Su 1:60-61 Bl * ;] 
a false witness: Matt.26:60; with genitive obj. (see WM, § 30, 1a), 1 Cor.15:15.†
 (AS)

G5576.d:
ψευδο-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Exod.20:16, Deu.5:20 (17) (עָנָה), Da TH Su 1:61 AB2R (see ψευδομάρτυς) * ;] 
to bear false witness: Matt.19:18, Mark.10:19, Luke.18:20" (LXX) ; before κατά, with genitive of person(s), Mark.14:56-57 (Xen., Plat., al.).†
 (AS)

G5578.d:
ψευδο-προφήτης, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Zec.13:2, Jer.1:9 (Jer.6:13, al.) (נָבִיא)* ;] 
a false prophet (= cl. ψευδόμαντις): Matt.7:15 24:11, 24, Mark.13:22 (see Swete, in l), Luke.6:26, Acts.13:6, 2 Pet.2:1, 1 John.4:1, Rev.16:13 19:20 20:10 †
 (AS)

G5579.d:
ψεῦδος, -εος (-ους), τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶר, also for כַּחַשׁ, כָּזָב ;] 
a falsehood, untruth, lie: Rev.14:15; opposite to ἡ ἀλήθεια, John.8:44, Rom.1:25, Eph.4:25, 2 Thess.2:11, 1 John.2:21; to τὸ ἀληθές, 1 John.2:27; ποιεῖν ψ., Rev.21:27 22:15; ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει κ. σημείοις κ. τέρασιν ψεύδους (genitive qual., see M, Th., 104; and on the meaning and construction, see also ICC, in l), 2 Thess.2:9.†
 (AS)

G5580.d:
ψευδό-χριστος, -ου ὁ 
 a false Christ or Messiah, "a pretender to the  Messianic office" (Swete, Mk., 309; cf. also Tr., Syn., § xxx): Matt.24:24, Mark.13:22 (cf. ἀντίχριστος).†
 (AS)

G5581.d:
ψευδώνυμος, -ον
 (ψευδής, ὄνομα) 
under a false name, falsely called: 1 Tim.6:20 (Æsch., Plut., a1.).†

G5582.d:
ψεῦσμα, -τος, τό
 (ψεύδω), [in Aq., Th.: Job.34:6, Pro.23:3; in Sm.: Job.13:4, al. ;]

G5583.d:
ψεύστης, -ου, ὁ

a liar: John.8:44, 55, Rom.3:4, 1 Tim.1:10, Titus.1:12, 1 John.1:10 Jn 2:4 Jn 2:22 Jn 4:20 Jn 5:10 .†

G5584.d:
ψηλαφάω, -ῶ
 (ψάω, to touch), [in LXX for מוּשׁ, מָשַׁשׁ pi., etc. ;] 
  1. to feel or grope about; with accusative, to feel about for, search after: metaphorically, of seeking God, Acts.17:27.

G5585.d:
ψηφίζω
 (ψῆφος), [in LXX: 3Ki.3:8 8:5 A (סָפַר ni..) * ;] 
to count (prop., with pebbles), reckon, calculate: τ. δαπάνην, Luke.14:28; τ. ἀριθμόν (i.e. calculate the number's meaning), Rev.13:18 (in cl. chiefly mid., to vote by casting a pebble; cf. συγ-κατα-, συμ-φηφίζω).†

G5586.d:
ψῆφος, -ου, ἡ

  1. a small smooth stone, a pebble: ψ. λευκή (for suggestions as to the meaning, see Swete, in l), Rev.2:17. 
  2. From the use of pebbles in voting, a vote: Acts.26:10.†

ψιθυριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
 (see supr.),

 Syn.: καταλάλος, q.v

ψιχίον, -ου, τό

G5590.d:
ψυχή, -ῆς, ἡ, 
 [in LXX very frequently for נֶפֶשׁ, sometimes for לֵבַב ,לֵב, etc. ;] 
  1. breath (Lat. anima), breath of life, life (Hom., al.; in Arist., of the vital principle): Matt.6:25, Mark.3:4 10:45, Luke.12:22, John.10:11, Acts.20:10, 24 2 Cor.1:23, Phil.2:30, 1 Thess.2:8, al. 
  2. the soul, 
  (a) as the seat of the will, desires and affections: Matt.26:38, Mark.12:30" (LXX) 14:34, Luke.1:46, John.10:24, Acts.14:2, Phil.1:27, al.; ἐκ ψυχῆς, from the heart, heartily: Eph.6:6, Col.3:23; 
  (b) as a periphrasis for person or self (frequently in  translation from Semitic originals, see M, Pr., 87; Robinson, Gospels, 113ff.; but also frequently in cl., see LS, see word II, 2; Edwards, Lex., App. A.): Matt.11:29, Mark.8:36, Acts.2:41, Rom.2:9, 1 Pet.3:20, al.; πᾶσα ψ., Acts.2:43 3:23" (LXX), Rom.13:1; ψ. ζῶσα (ζωῆς), 1 Cor.15:45, Rev.16:3; 
  (with) as the object of divine grace and eternal salvation: Heb.13:17, Jas.1:21 5:20, 1 Pet.1:9, 22 2:11 4:19, 3Jo.2. 
 SYN.: see: νοῦς, πνεῦμα, ψυχικός, and cf. ICC on 1 Thess.5:23, Lft., Notes, 88f. (AS)

G5591.d:
ψυχικός, -ή, -όν
 (ψυχή) [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 * ;] 
of the ψυχή (as the lower part of the immaterial in man), EV, natural: opposite to πνευματικός, 1 Cor.2:14 15:44 15:46; πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες (EV, sensual; R, mg., natural or animal; better perhaps, of the mind; see infr.), Ju 19; with ἐπίγειος, δαιμονιώδης, opposite to ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (σοψία), of the mind (Hort, in l), Jas.3:15†
 (AS)

G5592.d:
ψύχος (LT, ψῦ-, as in cl.), -εος (-ους), τό 
 (ψύχω), [in LXX: Gen.8:22 (קֹר), Job.37:9, Ps.147:17 (קָרָה), Zec.14:6, Dan LXX TH 3:67,69 * ;] 
cold: John.18:18, Acts.28:2, 2 Cor.11:27.†

ψυχρός, -ά, -όν
 (ψύχω), [in LXX: Pro.25:25 (קַר), Sir.43:20, 4Ma.11:26 * ;] 
cold: sc. ὕδωρ (cf. Theogn., 263; Hdt., ii, 37), Matt.10:42; metaphorically, of indifferent persons, Rev.3:15-16 †

G5594.d:
ψύχω 
 [in LXX for קוּר, שָׁטַח ;] 
to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaphorically, Matt.24:12.†
 (AS)

G5595.d:
ψωμίζω
 (ψωμός, a morsel), [in LXX chiefly for אָכַל hi. ;] 
to feed with morsels (as children or the sick; Hippocr.), hence, generally, in late writers, to feed, nourish: with accusative of person(s), Rom.12:20 (LXX); with accusative of thing(s), to give out for food, 1 Cor.13:3 (cf. WM, § 32, 4an; for dupl. accusative, cf. Num.11:4, Sir.15:3, al.).†
 (AS)

G5596.d:
ψωμίον, -ου, τό 
 dimin. of ψωμός, a fragment, morsel: John.13:26-27, 30.†
 (AS)

G5597.d:
ψώχω
 (ψώω, collat. form of ψάω, to rub) 
to rub: Luke.6:1.†
 (AS)

G5598.d:
Ω, ω, ὦ μέγα (cf. ὂ μικρόν), 
 omega, ô, the twenty-fourth and last letter. As a numeral, ω᾽ = 800, ω, = 800,000. As a symbol of the last (= τὸ τέλος), τὸ Ὦ (Rec. Ω, L, ὦ, T, ω), the Omega: Rev.1:8 21:6 22:13 (cf. Ἄλφα).†
 (AS)

G5600.d:
εἰμί, 
 with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be. 
  I. As substantive verb. 
  1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Acts.17:28, John.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1 Cor.1:28. 
  2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Matt.24:3, Mark.14:2, 15:42, Luke.21:23, John.4:6, 23, 5:10, al. 
  3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Matt.2:13, 15, Mark.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luke.1:80, 5:29, John.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mark.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Matt.1:20, 21:25, Mark.11:30, John.3:31, al. 
  4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.; 
  (a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Matt.16:28, Luke.16:19, John.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Matt.16:22, Luke.1:7, John.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Matt.16:28, 19:2, Mark.9:1, al.; 
  (b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1 Cor.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
  II. As copula uniting subject and predicate. 
  1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Matt.5:13, 14:15, Luke.1:18, 19, John.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
  2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Matt.13:19, 1 Cor.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Matt.27:46, Mark.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mark.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Matt.26:26-28, Mark.14:22, 24, Luke.22:19, 1 Cor.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.). 
  3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mark.5:42, Luke.3:23, 1 Cor.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1 Tim.1:20, 2 Tim.1:15; poss., Matt.5:3, 10, Mark.12:7, Luke.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1 Cor.1:12, 2 Cor.10:7, 2 Tim.2:19. 
  4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Acts.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1 Cor.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al. 
  5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.); 
  (a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Matt.10:30, Luke.9:32, John.3:24, Acts.21:35, 1 Cor.15:19, al; 
  (b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Matt.7:29, Mark.1:22, Luke.4:31, 14:1, Acts.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
  (with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luke.23:9.
  6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Matt.19:5, Mark.10:8, Heb.8:10, al. 
  7. C. adv.: Matt.19:20, Mark.4:26, Luke.18:11, al. 
  8. Ellipses; 
  (a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Matt.8:29, 24:32, John.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
  (b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Matt.14:27, Mark.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mark.13:6, John.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
 (AS)

Ἰωβήδ (WH, -βήλ, Lk, l.with; Rec., RV, Ὠβήδ), ὁ, indecl., 
 Jo bed (Obed): Matt.1:5, Luke.3:32.†
 (AS)

G5602.d:
ὧδε, adv., 
 [in LXX for חֲלֹם ,פֹּה ,הִנֶּה, etc. ;] 
  1. prop., of manner, so (Hom., al.). 
  2. In poets (rarely) and late writers, of place,

ᾠδή, -ῆς, ή 
 [in LXX chiefly for שִׁיר ;] 
a song, ode, whether sad or joyful; in LXX and NT always in praise of God or Christ: Rev.5:9 14:3 15:3; ᾠ πνευματικαί Eph.5:19, Col.3:16.†
 (AS)

G5604.d:
ὠδίν
 (late form of ὠδίς), -ῖνος, ἡ [in LXX for חֵבֶל חֶבֶל (and wrongly for חֶבֶל חֶבֶל, cf. Ac, l.with), חִיל, etc. ;]

G5605.d:
ὠδίνω 
 [in LXX chiefly for חוּל, also for חָבַל pi., etc. ;] 
to have birthpangs, to travail: Gal.4:27 (LXX), Rev.12:2; metaphorically, Gal.4:19 (cf. συν-ωδίνω).†

G5606.d:
ὦμος, οὐ, ὁ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for שְׁכֶם, כָּתֵף ;] 
the shoulder: Matt.23:4, Luke.15:5.†
 (AS)

G5607.d:
εἰμί, 
 with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be. 
  I. As substantive verb. 
  1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Acts.17:28, John.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1 Cor.1:28. 
  2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Matt.24:3, Mark.14:2, 15:42, Luke.21:23, John.4:6, 23, 5:10, al. 
  3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Matt.2:13, 15, Mark.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luke.1:80, 5:29, John.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mark.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Matt.1:20, 21:25, Mark.11:30, John.3:31, al. 
  4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.; 
  (a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Matt.16:28, Luke.16:19, John.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Matt.16:22, Luke.1:7, John.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Matt.16:28, 19:2, Mark.9:1, al.; 
  (b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1 Cor.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
  II. As copula uniting subject and predicate. 
  1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Matt.5:13, 14:15, Luke.1:18, 19, John.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
  2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Matt.13:19, 1 Cor.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Matt.27:46, Mark.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mark.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Matt.26:26-28, Mark.14:22, 24, Luke.22:19, 1 Cor.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.). 
  3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mark.5:42, Luke.3:23, 1 Cor.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1 Tim.1:20, 2 Tim.1:15; poss., Matt.5:3, 10, Mark.12:7, Luke.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1 Cor.1:12, 2 Cor.10:7, 2 Tim.2:19. 
  4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Acts.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1 Cor.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al. 
  5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.); 
  (a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Matt.10:30, Luke.9:32, John.3:24, Acts.21:35, 1 Cor.15:19, al; 
  (b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Matt.7:29, Mark.1:22, Luke.4:31, 14:1, Acts.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
  (with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luke.23:9.
  6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Matt.19:5, Mark.10:8, Heb.8:10, al. 
  7. C. adv.: Matt.19:20, Mark.4:26, Luke.18:11, al. 
  8. Ellipses; 
  (a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Matt.8:29, 24:32, John.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
  (b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Matt.14:27, Mark.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mark.13:6, John.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
 (AS)

G5610.d:
ὥρα, -ας, ἡ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for עֵת and in Da for שָׁעָה ;] 
  1. any time or period fixed by nature, esp. a season (Hom., Hdt., Plat., al.). 
  2. A part of the day, and esp. a twelfth part of day or night, an hour: Matt.24:36, Mark.13:32, Acts.10:3, al.; accus. in ans. to "when"? (M, Pr., 63, 215; Bl., §34, 8), John.4:52, Acts.10:3, 30 1 Cor.15:30, Rev.3:3; accusative of duration, Matt.20:12 26, Mark.14:37; inexactly, πρὸς ὥραν, for a season, for a time, John.5:35, 2 Cor.7:8, Gal.2:5; πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας, for a short season (ICC, in l.), 1 Thess.2:17. 
  3. A definite point of time, time, hour: Matt.26:45; with genitive of thing(s), Luke.1:10 14:17, Rev.3:10, al.; with genitive of person(s), Luke.22:53, John.2:4 7:30, al.; ἡ ἄρτι ὥρα, 1 Cor.4:11; ἐσχάτη ὥ., 1 John.2:18; before ὅτε, John.4:21, 23 5:25 16:25; ἵνα, John.12:23, al.; with accusative and inf., Rom.13:11 (cf. DB, ext., 475b 476b). 
 (AS)

G5611.d:
ὡραῖος, -α, -ον

G5612.d:

G5613.d:
ὡς, adverbial form of the relative pron. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ. 
  I. As relat. adv. of manner, as, like as, just as, even as; 
  1. with a demonstrative, like οὕτως, expressed or understood: οὕτως . . . ὡς, Mark.4:26, 1 Cor.3:15, Eph.5:28, Jas.2:12, al.; ὡς . . . οὕτως, Acts.8:32, 1 Cor.7:17, al.; elliptically (sc. οὕτως, οὕτω), with nom., Matt.6:29, al.; with accusative, Matt.19:19, Mark.12:31, al.; with prep., Matt.26:55, Mark.14:48, Luke.22:52, John.7:10, al.; with verb., John.15:6, 2 Cor.3:1, Eph.2:3, 1 Thess.5:6, al.; with ptcp. (the ptcp. however not having the special force wh. it has in cl.; see Bl., §73, 5; 74, 6), Matt.7:29, Mark.1:22, Heb.13:17, al.; freq implying opinion or belief, Rom.9:32;  so esp, with genitive absol., 1 Cor.4:18, 2 Cor.5:20, 1 Pet.4:12, 2 Pet.1:3. 
  2. Before numerals, about, nearly: Mark.5:13, John.1:40, Acts.5:7, al. 
  3. Before adjectives and adverbs, how: Rom.10:15 11:33, 1 Thess.2:10; with superl., ὡς τάχιστα, as quickly as possible, Acts.17:15. 
  
  II. As conjunction; 
  1. temporal, 
  (a) as, when, since: Mark.9:21 14:72, Luke.1:23, John.2:9, al.; 
  (b) while, when, as long as: Luke.12:58, John.12:36, Gal.6:10 (Field, Notes, 191); ὡς ἄν (M, Pr., 167, and see: ἄν), Rom.15:24, 1 Cor.11:34, Phil.2:23. 
  2. Final, in order that; with inf., in order to (M, Pr., 204n), Luke.9:52, Acts.20:24, Heb.7:9. 
 (AS)
